Sensei Hoshi|Welcome, young trader! I am.key: Sensei Hoshi|Welcome, young trader! I am Sensei Hoshi , master of this dojo. You wish to learn the ancient art of trading ? Then listen well!

Sensei Hoshi|A market is simply a place.key: Sensei Hoshi|A market is simply a place where people buy and sell things. A school card-trading club is a market! Some kids want to buy a rare card, some want to sell one.

Kitsu the Fox|And here's the secret, kya.key: Kitsu the Fox|And here's the secret, kya~! Prices move because of buyers and sellers . If LOTS of kids want the rare dragon card, its price goes UP ! If everyone wants to sell it... price goes DOWN !

Sensei Hoshi|Now, the special scroll of.key: Sensei Hoshi|Now, the special scroll of this dojo: the futures contract . It is a promise to buy or sell something at a set price on a future day.

Sensei Hoshi|Imagine you tell your frien.key: Sensei Hoshi|Imagine you tell your friend: 'Next Friday, I promise to trade you my dragon card for 10 Koins — no matter what!' That promise itself becomes valuable. If the dragon card becomes super popular by Thursday, your friend's promise to get it for only 10 Koins is a treasure!

Rival Kazuo|Heh. And real traders don't.key: Rival Kazuo|Heh. And real traders don't even wait until Friday. They buy and sell the promises themselves , all day long. Corn, gold, oil, stock indexes — there are futures for all of them.

Sensei Hoshi|In this dojo you will tame.key: Sensei Hoshi|In this dojo you will tame two legendary beasts. First: NQ — the Nasdaq-100 futures , the Lightning Stallion. It follows 100 giant tech companies and charges FAST — prices near 21,500 , leaping dozens of points in minutes!

Kitsu the Fox|And second: GC \u2014 Gold.key: Kitsu the Fox|And second: GC — Gold futures , the Golden Dragon, kya~! The ancient treasure beast, trading near 3,350 an ounce. Usually calmer than NQ... but when the world gets scared, gold ROARS! Real traders watch exactly these two.

Sensei Hoshi|We will train as intraday t.key: Sensei Hoshi|We will train as intraday traders — also called day traders . Our rule: every trade opens and closes on the same day . Like a ninja mission that must finish before sunset!

Sensei Hoshi|One more thing, and it is t.key: Sensei Hoshi|One more thing, and it is the most important scroll of all: in this dojo we use pretend Koins . Real futures trading is very risky and only for trained adults. Master the art here first. Now — to your first quiz!

Sensei Hoshi|To trade, you must read the.key: Sensei Hoshi|To trade, you must read the market's secret language: the candlestick chart . Each candle tells the story of the price during a short time — like one panel in a manga!

Sensei Hoshi|A candle has a thick body a.key: Sensei Hoshi|A candle has a thick body and thin wicks on top and bottom. The body shows where the price opened and where it closed .

Kitsu the Fox|Color code, kya~! A green.key: Kitsu the Fox|Color code, kya~! A green candle means the price went UP during that time — the heroes won that battle! A red candle means the price went DOWN — the bears won.

Sensei Hoshi|The wicks are the shadows o.key: Sensei Hoshi|The wicks are the shadows of the battle. The top wick shows the highest price reached; the bottom wick shows the lowest . A long wick means the price tried to go there... but got pushed back!

Rival Kazuo|Pro tip: one candle is one p.key: Rival Kazuo|Pro tip: one candle is one panel, but the whole chart is the story . Lots of big green candles in a row? Buyers are powerful today. Lots of red? Sellers rule.

Sensei Hoshi|In our dojo's chart, each c.key: Sensei Hoshi|In our dojo's chart, each candle is a few minutes of the trading day. Watch them form, one by one, and you will feel the market's rhythm. Quiz time, then your first dojo mission awaits!

Sensei Hoshi|Today you learn the way of.key: Sensei Hoshi|Today you learn the way of the trend . A trend is the direction the market is traveling — like a river's current.

Sensei Hoshi|An uptrend makes higher hil.key: Sensei Hoshi|An uptrend makes higher hills and higher valleys — climbing a mountain. A downtrend makes lower hills and lower valleys — sliding down. And sometimes the market moves sideways , just resting.

Kitsu the Fox|The ancient surfing wisdom.key: Kitsu the Fox|The ancient surfing wisdom, kya~: the trend is your friend! It is much easier to ride the wave than to swim against it!

Sensei Hoshi|This is why traders can pro.key: Sensei Hoshi|This is why traders can profit in BOTH directions. Going LONG means you buy first, hoping the price rises. Going SHORT means you sell first, hoping the price falls — then you buy it back cheaper. With futures, both are normal moves!

Rival Kazuo|Short selling blew my mind t.key: Rival Kazuo|Short selling blew my mind too. Think of it like this: you promise to deliver a card later, sell that promise for 12 Koins today, and when the card's price drops to 8, you grab one and deliver it. You keep the 4 Koin difference. Sneaky... but fair!

Sensei Hoshi|Two more words of power: su.key: Sensei Hoshi|Two more words of power: support is a floor where falling prices often bounce up. Resistance is a ceiling where rising prices often get rejected. Watch where the price bounced before — it remembers!

Sensei Hoshi|Your mission in the dojo: w.key: Sensei Hoshi|Your mission in the dojo: watch the candles, find the wave's direction, and ride it. LONG in an uptrend, SHORT in a downtrend. Now prove your knowledge!

Sensei Hoshi|Listen closely, for this is.key: Sensei Hoshi|Listen closely, for this is the most important arc of your entire training . Every anime hero needs armor. A trader's armor is called risk management .

Sensei Hoshi|Truth one: nobody wins ever.key: Sensei Hoshi|Truth one: nobody wins every trade. Not me, not the greatest market samurai in history. Losing some trades is normal — like losing some battles in a long tournament arc.

Kitsu the Fox|So the real question isn't.key: Kitsu the Fox|So the real question isn't 'how do I never lose?' It's 'how do I keep my losses SMALL?' Small scratches heal fast. Giant wounds end the adventure, kya~!

Sensei Hoshi|Behold the legendary shield.key: Sensei Hoshi|Behold the legendary shield: the STOP-LOSS . When you open a trade, you set a line: 'If the price hits HERE, close my trade automatically.' It cuts a losing trade while the loss is still tiny.

Rival Kazuo|I learned this the hard way..key: Rival Kazuo|I learned this the hard way. Once I skipped my shield because I was SURE I was right. The market didn't care how sure I was. Now I never trade without a stop-loss. Never.

Sensei Hoshi|Rule of the dojo: risk only.key: Sensei Hoshi|Rule of the dojo: risk only a small slice of your Koins on any one trade. Grown-up traders often risk just 1–2% per trade. Then even five losses in a row is just a training montage — not game over.

Sensei Hoshi|And beware the double-edged.key: Sensei Hoshi|And beware the double-edged sword of futures: leverage . It makes wins bigger AND losses bigger. That is exactly why real futures are for trained adults only — and why the shield matters above all. Quiz, then the Shield Trial awaits in the dojo!

Sensei Hoshi|You have learned candles, w.key: Sensei Hoshi|You have learned candles, waves, and the shield. But the final enemies are not on the chart. They live inside the trader's own mind .

Sensei Hoshi|Demon one: FOMO \u2014 the.key: Sensei Hoshi|Demon one: FOMO — the Fear Of Missing Out. The price rockets up, your heart screams 'JUMP IN NOW!' ... usually right before it falls back down. The patient ninja waits for the next proper setup.

Rival Kazuo|Demon two: Revenge Trading ..key: Rival Kazuo|Demon two: Revenge Trading . You lose a trade, get angry, and instantly slam into another trade to 'win it back.' That's not a strategy — that's the demon driving. After a loss: breathe, review, reset.

Kitsu the Fox|Demon three: Overtrading ,.key: Kitsu the Fox|Demon three: Overtrading , kya~! Trading every wiggle because sitting still feels boring. But a sniper takes few shots — the best traders spend most of the day just watching .

Sensei Hoshi|The weapon against all thre.key: Sensei Hoshi|The weapon against all three demons is the trading plan . Before you trade, decide: Why am I entering? Where is my shield? When will I take profit? Then follow the plan like a sacred scroll.

Sensei Hoshi|And honor the trading journ.key: Sensei Hoshi|And honor the trading journal — after each dojo day, ask: did I follow my plan? Heroes level up by reviewing their battles, not just fighting them.

Sensei Hoshi|Remember: a good trade is o.key: Sensei Hoshi|Remember: a good trade is one where you followed your plan — even if it lost. A bad trade is breaking your rules — even if you got lucky and won. Discipline IS the superpower. Final quiz, then the boss awaits!

Sensei Hoshi|Young trader... you have co.key: Sensei Hoshi|Young trader... you have come far. Candles, trends, the shield, the calm mind. One trial remains: the Volatility Dragon .

Kitsu the Fox|Volatility means how wildl.key: Kitsu the Fox|Volatility means how wildly the price jumps around , kya~! Some days the market is a sleepy pond. Dragon days, it's a stormy ocean — huge candles, sudden reversals!

Sensei Hoshi|On wild days, the wise trad.key: Sensei Hoshi|On wild days, the wise trader adapts: trade smaller, keep the shield closer to your heart, and be pickier about which battles to fight. Wild markets give bigger chances — and bigger dangers.

Rival Kazuo|This is your graduation batt.key: Rival Kazuo|This is your graduation battle. Everything you've learned, all at once. Ride the waves, wear your shield, keep your mind calm even when the dragon roars. I'll be watching, rival. Don't lose.

Sensei Hoshi|Pass the final quiz, then e.key: Sensei Hoshi|Pass the final quiz, then enter the dojo for the Boss Battle . Survive the dragon's storm and finish the day with profit — and you shall be named a Legendary Trade Master . Go forth!

Sensei Hoshi|You thought your training e.key: Sensei Hoshi|You thought your training ended with the dragon? Ha! True masters never stop learning. Welcome to the Strategy Saga — where feelings retire and exact rules take command.

Sensei Hoshi|A strategy is a set of rule.key: Sensei Hoshi|A strategy is a set of rules decided BEFORE the battle: when to enter, where the shield goes, when to leave. Rules protect you from your own excited heart.

Sensei Hoshi|Rule scroll one: the Openin.key: Sensei Hoshi|Rule scroll one: the Opening Range . Every morning the market fights its first battle. The first candles of the day draw the battlefield — the highest point is the Range High , the lowest is the Range Low .

Kitsu the Fox|And when the price SMASHES.key: Kitsu the Fox|And when the price SMASHES out of that range — that's the breakout , kya~! Bulls breaking the ceiling often keep charging UP. Bears breaking the floor often keep tumbling DOWN. Traders call this the ORB — Opening Range Breakout!

Rival Kazuo|But watch for fake-outs : pr.key: Rival Kazuo|But watch for fake-outs : price pokes one toe out of the range, then dives right back in. I've been fooled plenty. That's exactly why one clue is never enough...

Sensei Hoshi|Rule scroll two: the Gap ..key: Sensei Hoshi|Rule scroll two: the Gap . Sometimes price leaps so fast it skips a stair, leaving an empty zone on the chart — traders call it a fair value gap , or a DEM (magnet) or a BIM (Balance/Imbalance Mark)!

Sensei Hoshi|The market LOVES to be bala.key: Sensei Hoshi|The market LOVES to be balanced and fair . A fast, one-sided move leaves an unfair empty gap. So the market feels pulled to come back and fill it. That's why price has a GOAL — it isn't wandering, it's being pulled to a magnet!

Kitsu the Fox|BIMs and DEMs act like sup.key: Kitsu the Fox|BIMs and DEMs act like support and resistance, kya~! To find a BIM, connect the high of the wick of candle 1 to the low of the wick of candle 3 in an uptrend (or low of candle 1 to high of candle 3 in a downtrend). The empty space between them is the gap!

Rival Kazuo|When price reaches a goal, D.key: Rival Kazuo|When price reaches a goal, Dad watches bodies first, wicks second . Price needs a candle body (close) beyond the level to keep going. If it only pokes its nose (wick) past and fails to close, it will bounce back!

Kitsu the Fox|Here is Dad's favorite tri.key: Kitsu the Fox|Here is Dad's favorite trick, kya~! When price dips into a DEM/BIM, it's like stopping at a gas station to refuel. It usually only needs to dip halfway (50%) or at most three-quarters (75%) to get GAS and turn around. Deeper than that? The gas tank might be leaking!

Sensei Hoshi|Rule scroll three: the Wall.key: Sensei Hoshi|Rule scroll three: the Walls . The market remembers! Yesterday's high and low are walls in its memory. Breaking through a wall is a powerful sign — far stronger than wiggles in the middle of nowhere.

Sensei Hoshi|Now the secret that binds t.key: Sensei Hoshi|Now the secret that binds them: CONFLUENCE . One clue is a rumor. Two clues is a hint. Three clues pointing the same way is a plan! Breakout + Gap + Wall, all agreeing — that is when a strategist strikes.

Kitsu the Fox|In the dojo, your chart no.key: Kitsu the Fox|In the dojo, your chart now shows all of it: the range zone, the gap boxes, the walls — and three signal lamps that light up as clues align. When all three glow the same direction... kya~!

Sensei Hoshi|Remember: a strategy does n.key: Sensei Hoshi|Remember: a strategy does not win every battle — it wins the war by giving you an edge and keeping the demons out. Quiz time, then hunt the breakout!

Sensei Hoshi|One final scroll, and it ma.key: Sensei Hoshi|One final scroll, and it may protect you more than all the others combined. There is a demon that lives inside phones. I call it... the Hype Demon .

Rival Kazuo|I met it once. A video: 'My.key: Rival Kazuo|I met it once. A video: 'My trading bot made 2,000 gold in THIRTY MINUTES!' My heart raced. I almost sent the stranger my Koins to learn his secret. Then Sensei made me watch the video again... carefully.

Sensei Hoshi|Listen closely to such vide.key: Sensei Hoshi|Listen closely to such videos and you find the hidden truths: the same trader lost 2,000 gold three days earlier . His bot was broken for a week. It traded twice when it planned ten. Social media shows the highlight reel — never the report card.

Kitsu the Fox|The Hype Demon's favorite.key: Kitsu the Fox|The Hype Demon's favorite tricks, kya~! Promises of easy money. Only wins shown, never losses. Big numbers + short time. 'Secret strategy' for sale. 'Almost funded, trust me!' Spot one flag, look for the rest!

Sensei Hoshi|Now the deepest wisdom: sam.key: Sensei Hoshi|Now the deepest wisdom: sample size . Flip a coin three times and get three heads — is the coin magic? Of course not! One green day proves NOTHING. A real strategy is judged over many, many trades — like a season, not one match.

Sensei Hoshi|So what does a wise trader.key: Sensei Hoshi|So what does a wise trader do with a shiny new strategy? Test before trust. Try it with pretend Koins, many times, write down every result — wins AND losses — and judge the whole table. That is called being a scientist .

Sensei Hoshi|Your final mission awaits:.key: Sensei Hoshi|Your final mission awaits: the Strategy Scientist trial — five trading days, one strategy, honest results. You pass by following the method , not by getting lucky. Win or lose, the scientist always learns. Now, the quiz!

Sensei Hoshi|One final secret map, young.key: Sensei Hoshi|One final secret map, young sage. Liquidity means how many orders are waiting to trade at each price. Some prices are quiet ponds... others are deep treasure pools full of resting orders.

Sensei Hoshi|Pools form at the famous le.key: Sensei Hoshi|Pools form at the famous levels every trader watches — especially yesterday's battle marks : PDH (Previous Day High), PDL (Previous Day Low), PDO (Previous Day Open), and PDC (Previous Day Close).

Kitsu the Fox|And don't forget the middl.key: Kitsu the Fox|And don't forget the middle of yesterday's range — PD 50% , the equilibrium , kya~! Above it, buyers feel strong. Below it, sellers rule. Five magic lines you can draw before the day even begins !

Rival Kazuo|Dad also marks special sessi.key: Rival Kazuo|Dad also marks special session candle times on the 15-minute chart: Previous Day Close ( PDC / 4:45 PM), London Open prep ( 2:45 AM ), News opening ( 8:30 AM ), and Market Open prep ( 9:15 AM ).

Rival Kazuo|Why? Because the market love.key: Rival Kazuo|Why? Because the market loves to sweep (poke past) one side of these session candle ranges to trap eager retail traders in a trapdoor. Once the shields (stop orders) are gobbled up... SNAP, price reverses! That's a liquidity sweep .

Sensei Hoshi|So the wise trader never ch.key: Sensei Hoshi|So the wise trader never chases price into a pool. Watch the reaction instead: a sweep followed by a snap-back tells you the pool is empty — the move may be done, and the snap-back may be the real trade.

Sensei Hoshi|This is also the deep truth.key: Sensei Hoshi|This is also the deep truth of support and resistance : support is a floor of waiting buyers; resistance is a ceiling of waiting sellers. And the great secret — when a ceiling truly breaks, it often becomes a floor. The role flip !

Kitsu the Fox|In the dojo's Liquidity Hu.key: Kitsu the Fox|In the dojo's Liquidity Hunter mission, all five lines are drawn for you, with the pools glowing beyond PDH and PDL. When a sweep happens, the log shouts and the chart shakes, kya~!

Sensei Hoshi|Remember the creed: levels.key: Sensei Hoshi|Remember the creed: levels are magnets and walls, sweeps are traps for the impatient, and reactions are the truth. Take the quiz — then go fish where the fish are!

Sensei Hoshi|Young trader\u2026 you have.key: Sensei Hoshi|Young trader… you have learned every ingredient. Now I hand you your father's own recipe — the one checklist he runs every single time. B.R.E.A.D = Behavior, Reaction, Execution, Alignment, Discipline. This is exactly how Dad trades — one way, every trade.

Sensei Hoshi|B \u2014 Behavior (The Idea.key: Sensei Hoshi|B — Behavior (The Idea). Higher timeframe (HTF) is KING (4h/1h). Check it every single hour! Mark respected zones at the highs and lows. Say: 'I want to see price get HERE.' That is your Behavior target.

Kitsu the Fox|Dad's iron rule: only mark.key: Kitsu the Fox|Dad's iron rule: only mark zones that did something NEW ! It must have taken out a fresh swing point (a hill higher than the trees to its left and right, never touched before). If a zone didn't do something new, it is weak!

Rival Kazuo|If a zone is weak and didn't.key: Rival Kazuo|If a zone is weak and didn't do something new, when price returns, it won't hold. Price runs straight through it like a bowling ball through paper cups! Dad calls this the 'Down Go Frazier!' rule. Don't mark them!

Kitsu the Fox|Then play it zone to zone.key: Kitsu the Fox|Then play it zone to zone . When price reaches a level, watch the candle close: if it rejects (bounces), price swings back to the previous zone. If it closes BEYOND (body close), the zone is beaten — on to the next zone! Bounce = back, break = onward.

Rival Kazuo|If price leaps overnight and.key: Rival Kazuo|If price leaps overnight and leaves a GAP , it acts like a breakout-retest: price dips back to fill the gap, grabs GAS (about halfway in), then continues. Mark it from the body of the last candle before the jump.

Sensei Hoshi|R \u2014 Reaction (The Wait.key: Sensei Hoshi|R — Reaction (The Wait). When price reaches your zone, NEVER enter the instant it touches! Wait for the candle to CLOSE on the small timeframe and show a reaction (like a hammer, wick, or failed push). No close + reaction = NO TRADE!

Sensei Hoshi|E \u2014 Execution (The set.key: Sensei Hoshi|E — Execution (The setups). Only trade Dad's two setups (the **BNRs**): ① Bounce & Reject (his favorite) at the outer highs/lows of a range — never the middle. ② Break & Retest . Play the second move , not the first! Price always comes back for you.

Rival Kazuo|A \u2014 Alignment (The Maps.key: Rival Kazuo|A — Alignment (The Maps). Make sure your maps agree. The 2-minute chart might look ready, but if the 15-minute and 1-hour maps say NO, you are not aligned. Only trade in the direction of the Higher Timeframe!

Rival Kazuo|Your stop-loss goes just bey.key: Rival Kazuo|Your stop-loss goes just beyond the zone. If a candle closes past it , your idea is INVALID — cut the trade instantly! No hoping, no moving stops. Give the trade max 2½ hours to win; after that, let it go. Protect your Koins!

Sensei Hoshi|D \u2014 Discipline (The Ru.key: Sensei Hoshi|D — Discipline (The Rules). The strategy is nothing without YOU. Control your feelings, stay patient, stay calm. Remember: max 3 trades a session , no alert = no trade , no inside days. Follow this flowchart, and you shall claim the bread!

Sensei Hoshi|Before any chart, learn how.key: Sensei Hoshi|Before any chart, learn how the scoreboard counts. In futures you do not buy shares . You trade contracts — one contract is one ticket to ride the price.

Sensei Hoshi|Price moves in points . If.key: Sensei Hoshi|Price moves in points . If NQ goes from 21,500 to 21,510, it moved 10 points . That is the whole trick: count the points.

Kitsu the Fox|And the smallest hop price.key: Kitsu the Fox|And the smallest hop price can make is a tick , kya~! On NQ a tick is a quarter of a point — four ticks make one point . On Gold a tick is 10 cents.

Rival Kazuo|Here is where it gets real..key: Rival Kazuo|Here is where it gets real. Each point is worth money. On the big NQ contract, one point = $20 . On the small one, MNQ (the Micro), one point = $2 . Same chart, ten times smaller.

Rival Kazuo|Gold works the same way. On.key: Rival Kazuo|Gold works the same way. On big GC , a $1 move in gold = $100 . On Micro Gold, MGC , a $1 move = $10 . Beginners start on the Micros. Always.

Sensei Hoshi|So the scoreboard is one su.key: Sensei Hoshi|So the scoreboard is one sum: points × dollars-per-point × contracts . Ride MNQ for 10 points with 1 contract: 10 × $2 × 1 = $20 . With 5 contracts? $100 .

Sensei Hoshi|And it cuts both ways. Thos.key: Sensei Hoshi|And it cuts both ways. Those same 10 points against you is a $20 loss — or $100 with 5 contracts. NQ can move 60 points in two minutes. More contracts is not more skill. It is more speed.

Kitsu the Fox|That is why real traders d.key: Kitsu the Fox|That is why real traders decide the stop first and the size second, kya~! You will learn that properly in the Way of the Shield. For now: know your points, know what each one costs.

Sensei Hoshi|Every craft has its own lan.key: Sensei Hoshi|Every craft has its own language, and trading is no different. Learn these words now and no chart, video or trader will ever sound like a puzzle again.

Sensei Hoshi|Long means you buy first ,.key: Sensei Hoshi|Long means you buy first , hoping price goes up. Short means you sell first , hoping price goes down. In futures both are completely normal.

Kitsu the Fox|Bullish = price is pushing.key: Kitsu the Fox|Bullish = price is pushing UP, like a bull tossing its horns to the sky, kya~! Bearish = price is pushing DOWN, like a bear swiping its paw to the ground.

Rival Kazuo|Three places matter in every.key: Rival Kazuo|Three places matter in every trade. Your entry is where you get in. Your stop is where you get out if you are wrong. Your target is where you get out if you are right. Know all three before you click.

Sensei Hoshi|A timeframe is how much tim.key: Sensei Hoshi|A timeframe is how much time one candle holds. On a 1-hour chart each candle is one hour. On a 2-minute chart, two minutes. Big timeframes show the journey; small ones show the footsteps.

Sensei Hoshi|Support is a floor \u2014 a.key: Sensei Hoshi|Support is a floor — a price where falling stops and bounces. Resistance is a ceiling — a price where rising stops and turns back. Almost everything on a chart is one of these two.

Kitsu the Fox|A pullback is price taking.key: Kitsu the Fox|A pullback is price taking a little step backwards before it keeps going, kya~. A breakout is price smashing through a floor or ceiling. And a range is price stuck bouncing between the two.

Rival Kazuo|Last ones. P&L is your profi.key: Rival Kazuo|Last ones. P&L is your profit and loss — your score. Risk is what you lose if your stop gets hit. And R is one unit of that risk: risk $20 to make $60 and you made 3R .

Sensei Hoshi|You do not need to memorise.key: Sensei Hoshi|You do not need to memorise all of it today. The Words book is always open in the side menu — tap any word, any time. Now show me what stuck!

Sensei Hoshi|You can read one candle. No.key: Sensei Hoshi|You can read one candle. Now learn the candles that say something . Traders call them reaction candles — they show who won the fight at an important price.

Sensei Hoshi|The hammer : a small body a.key: Sensei Hoshi|The hammer : a small body at the top and a long wick underneath. Sellers shoved price way down… and buyers shoved it all the way back. At a floor, that is buyers saying not today .

Kitsu the Fox|Flip it upside down and yo.key: Kitsu the Fox|Flip it upside down and you get the shooting star , kya~! Small body at the bottom, long wick on top. Buyers reached up high and got slapped back down. At a ceiling, sellers are in charge.

Sensei Hoshi|The doji : almost no body a.key: Sensei Hoshi|The doji : almost no body at all. It opened and closed in nearly the same spot. Nobody won. A doji is the market holding its breath — the next candle tells you who breathes out first.

Rival Kazuo|The engulfing candle is my f.key: Rival Kazuo|The engulfing candle is my favourite. One big body completely swallows the body before it. Red candle, then a bigger green one that eats it? Buyers just took the wheel. The reverse means sellers did.

Rival Kazuo|And the sneaky one: the fail.key: Rival Kazuo|And the sneaky one: the failed break . A candle pokes above the last candle's high… then closes back down inside. It tried to go up and failed. That poke is a trap, and the snap-back is the tell.

Sensei Hoshi|One more shape, built from.key: Sensei Hoshi|One more shape, built from three candles: the swing point . A swing high is a candle whose high is taller than the candle before AND after it. A swing low is the opposite. These are the hills and valleys we mark.

Sensei Hoshi|Now the rule that matters m.key: Sensei Hoshi|Now the rule that matters most: a pattern only counts at a level . A hammer in the middle of nowhere is just a candle. A hammer sitting right on a floor you marked earlier? That is the market talking.

Kitsu the Fox|And never jump while the c.key: Kitsu the Fox|And never jump while the candle is still wiggling, kya~! It can look like a hammer with ten seconds left and finish as something else. Wait for the close. The close is the truth.

Sensei Hoshi|A trend is not a feeling. I.key: Sensei Hoshi|A trend is not a feeling. It is a staircase , and you can count the steps. Four little labels are all you need: HH, HL, LH, LL .

Sensei Hoshi|HH = Higher High: a hill ta.key: Sensei Hoshi|HH = Higher High: a hill taller than the last hill. HL = Higher Low: a valley that did not fall as far as the last valley.

Kitsu the Fox|Higher High, Higher Low, H.key: Kitsu the Fox|Higher High, Higher Low, Higher High, Higher Low — that is an uptrend , kya~! Stairs going UP. Buyers win each push and give back less each rest.

Rival Kazuo|Now the other way. LH = Lowe.key: Rival Kazuo|Now the other way. LH = Lower High: a hill shorter than the last one. LL = Lower Low: a valley deeper than the last. LH, LL, LH, LL — a downtrend . Stairs going down.

Sensei Hoshi|Here is the powerful part..key: Sensei Hoshi|Here is the powerful part. In an uptrend, the last Higher Low is the step holding everything up. As long as price stays above it, the staircase is alive. Buyers are still in charge.

Sensei Hoshi|But when a candle closes it.key: Sensei Hoshi|But when a candle closes its body below that Higher Low — the step snaps. The staircase is broken. Traders call it a break of structure , and it is the first warning the trend may be turning.

Rival Kazuo|Notice I said body . A wick.key: Rival Kazuo|Notice I said body . A wick poking through is just price sniffing around. A body closing beyond the level means price actually did something new. Bodies first, wicks second.

Kitsu the Fox|And when there are no clea.key: Kitsu the Fox|And when there are no clean stairs at all — highs and lows all jumbled up — that is a range , kya~. No staircase, no direction. The best traders just… wait.

Sensei Hoshi|So before every trade, ask.key: Sensei Hoshi|So before every trade, ask one question: which way are the stairs going? Buy in the up-staircase. Sell in the down-staircase. Never argue with the stairs.

Sensei Hoshi|NQ and Gold do not sleep wh.key: Sensei Hoshi|NQ and Gold do not sleep when you do. Futures trade almost all day and all night , from Sunday evening to Friday afternoon. But the market is not the same animal at every hour.

Sensei Hoshi|The day has three parts, na.key: Sensei Hoshi|The day has three parts, named for where the world is awake. First the Asia session — evening and night in New York, roughly 6 PM to 3 AM . It is usually the quiet one.

Kitsu the Fox|Asia mostly tiptoes sidewa.key: Kitsu the Fox|Asia mostly tiptoes sideways and builds a little box, kya~. Remember the top and bottom of that box — the Asia high and Asia low . Later sessions love to come back for them!

Rival Kazuo|Then London wakes up, around.key: Rival Kazuo|Then London wakes up, around 3 AM . Europe's traders pour in and the market stretches its legs. London often makes the first real move of the day — and often pokes past Asia's box to do it.

Sensei Hoshi|Then the main event: New Yo.key: Sensei Hoshi|Then the main event: New York . News often lands at 8:30 AM , and the stock market's opening bell rings at 9:30 AM . This is when NQ runs fastest. Most of our trading lives right here.

Kitsu the Fox|London and New York are bo.key: Kitsu the Fox|London and New York are both awake at the same time for a few hours in the morning, kya~. Two giant crowds trading at once! That overlap is the busiest, loudest part of the whole day — especially for Gold.

Rival Kazuo|After lunch things go sleepy.key: Rival Kazuo|After lunch things go sleepy… then comes Power Hour : 3 PM to 4 PM , the last hour before the closing bell. The big players finish their business for the day, and the market wakes up fast.

Sensei Hoshi|Here is the secret of the c.key: Sensei Hoshi|Here is the secret of the clock: each session hands off to the next . New York sets up Asia. Asia sets up London. London and Asia together set up the next New York. So every session, we look at the chart fresh.

Rival Kazuo|And watch the candle just be.key: Rival Kazuo|And watch the candle just before a session begins. Price loves to fake one way first — poke out, trap the eager ones — and then run the other way. First move: trick. Second move: truth.

Sensei Hoshi|So a wise trader does not j.key: Sensei Hoshi|So a wise trader does not just ask where is price. They ask what time is it? The same setup in sleepy Asia and at the New York open are two very different trades.

Sensei Hoshi|A chart with no lines is a.key: Sensei Hoshi|A chart with no lines is a map with no roads. Before the day begins, a trader draws a few key levels — the prices where something is most likely to happen.

Sensei Hoshi|Start with yesterday. PDH i.key: Sensei Hoshi|Start with yesterday. PDH is the Previous Day High — the highest price yesterday. PDL is the Previous Day Low — the lowest. Every trader on Earth can see these two.

Kitsu the Fox|Now draw the line exactly.key: Kitsu the Fox|Now draw the line exactly halfway between them: PD 50% , kya~! The middle of yesterday. Above it, buyers have the upper hand. Below it, sellers do. It is the tug-of-war line!

Rival Kazuo|Why do these matter so much?.key: Rival Kazuo|Why do these matter so much? Because crowds of traders park their orders — and their stops — right around them. Lots of orders in one spot is called liquidity . Price gets pulled toward it like a magnet.

Sensei Hoshi|The same trick works on big.key: Sensei Hoshi|The same trick works on bigger and smaller clocks. The previous week's high, low and 50%. The Asia high and low. The London high and low. Each one is a line the crowd is watching.

Sensei Hoshi|Then mark the hills and val.key: Sensei Hoshi|Then mark the hills and valleys on the big charts — the swing highs and swing lows on the 1-hour and 4-hour. And mark them at the candle bodies first. Where price closed is where the decision was made.

Rival Kazuo|Do NOT draw fifty lines. A m.key: Rival Kazuo|Do NOT draw fifty lines. A messy chart makes a nervous trader. Only mark a level if it has a story — a place where control clearly flipped. If two lines sit side by side, keep one.

Sensei Hoshi|Now the big rule of this wh.key: Sensei Hoshi|Now the big rule of this whole academy: take entries AT your levels, and take targets FROM your levels. Never trade in the empty middle between two lines. The middle is where beginners get chopped up.

Kitsu the Fox|And when price finally arr.key: Kitsu the Fox|And when price finally arrives at your line — do not jump, kya~! Arriving is only the knock on the door. Wait for the reaction candle to close. A bounce, a rejection, a failed break. Then it is go time.

Sensei Hoshi|E \u2014 Execution (The set.key: Sensei Hoshi|E — Execution (The setups). Only trade Dad's two setups (the BNRs ): ① Bounce & Reject (his favorite) at the outer highs/lows of a range — never the middle. ② Break & Retest . Play the second move , not the first! Price always comes back for you.

|Welcome. This course teaches trading fr.key: |Welcome. This course teaches trading from zero, one idea per screen, in the same order your child is learning it. No prior knowledge is assumed.

|A market is any place where people buy.key: |A market is any place where people buy and sell . A farmers' market, an auction site and a futures exchange all work on the same principle: some people want to buy, others want to sell.

|Prices move because of buyers and selle.key: |Prices move because of buyers and sellers . When more people want to buy than sell, the price goes up . When more want to sell than buy, it goes down .

|The instrument we trade here is the fut.key: |The instrument we trade here is the futures contract : a binding agreement to buy or sell something at a set price on a set future date.

|Suppose you agree today to buy somethin.key: |Suppose you agree today to buy something next Friday for 10, no matter what it is worth by then . If its market price rises to 15 by Thursday, your agreement to pay only 10 has become valuable in itself.

|In practice, traders rarely hold a cont.key: |In practice, traders rarely hold a contract until that date. They buy and sell the contracts themselves throughout the day. Futures exist for corn, gold, oil, stock indexes and much more.

|You will practice on two markets. The f.key: |You will practice on two markets. The first is NQ — Nasdaq-100 futures , which tracks 100 large technology-heavy companies. It moves fast: in the simulator it trades near 21,500 and can move dozens of points in minutes.

|The second is GC \u2014 Gold futures ,.key: |The second is GC — Gold futures , trading near 3,350 an ounce in the simulator. It is usually calmer than NQ, but it can move sharply when the world gets nervous. Many real traders watch exactly these two.

|We train as intraday traders , also cal.key: |We train as intraday traders , also called day traders . The rule: every trade is opened and closed on the same day . Nothing is held overnight.

|Most important of all: everything here.key: |Most important of all: everything here uses practice money ( Koins in the simulator). Real futures trading is high-risk and should only follow serious practice. Learn it here first, then take the quiz.

|Before reading a chart, learn how the m.key: |Before reading a chart, learn how the money is counted. In futures you do not buy shares. You trade contracts — one contract is one unit of exposure to the price.

|Price is measured in points . If NQ goe.key: |Price is measured in points . If NQ goes from 21,500 to 21,510, it moved 10 points . Every profit and loss starts as a number of points.

|The smallest step price can take is a t.key: |The smallest step price can take is a tick . On NQ a tick is 0.25 points, so four ticks make one point. On Gold a tick is $0.10.

|Each point has a dollar value. On the f.key: |Each point has a dollar value. On the full-size NQ contract one point is $20 . On MNQ , the Micro, one point is $2 . The chart is identical; the Micro is one tenth the size.

|Gold works the same way. On GC , a $1.0.key: |Gold works the same way. On GC , a $1.00 move in the gold price is $100 per contract. On MGC , Micro Gold, it is $10 . Beginners start on the Micros.

|So every result is one calculation: poi.key: |So every result is one calculation: points × dollars per point × contracts . Ten points on one MNQ contract is 10 × $2 × 1 = $20 . On five contracts it is $100 .

|It works identically against you. Ten p.key: |It works identically against you. Ten points the wrong way is a $20 loss on one MNQ, or $100 on five. NQ can move 60 points in two minutes. Adding contracts adds speed, not skill.

|This is why the stop is decided first a.key: |This is why the stop is decided first and the size second — covered properly in the risk world. For now: always know how many points are at stake and what each one costs.

|Trading has its own vocabulary. Learn i.key: |Trading has its own vocabulary. Learn it once and every chart, course and conversation becomes readable.

|Going long means buying first, to profi.key: |Going long means buying first, to profit if price rises. Going short means selling first, to profit if price falls. In futures both are routine.

|Bullish means price is pushing up, or y.key: |Bullish means price is pushing up, or you expect it to. Bearish means price is pushing down, or you expect it to.

|Every trade has three prices. The entry.key: |Every trade has three prices. The entry is where you get in. The stop is where you exit if you are wrong. The target is where you exit if you are right. All three are decided before you enter.

|A timeframe is the amount of time one c.key: |A timeframe is the amount of time one candle covers. A 1-hour chart shows the larger direction; a 2-minute chart shows the detail inside it. We call these higher and lower timeframes — HTF and LTF.

|Support is a price where a decline stop.key: |Support is a price where a decline stops and turns up. Resistance is a price where a rise stops and turns down. Almost every tool on a chart ends up acting as one of the two.

|A pullback is a temporary move against.key: |A pullback is a temporary move against the trend before it continues. A breakout is price moving through support or resistance. A range is price contained between the two.

|P&L is profit and loss. Risk is the amo.key: |P&L is profit and loss. Risk is the amount lost if the stop is hit. R is one unit of that risk — risking $20 to make $60 is a 3R trade.

|You do not need to memorise all of this.key: |You do not need to memorise all of this now. The Words glossary is always available from the side menu. A short quiz follows.

|To trade, you need to read a candlestic.key: |To trade, you need to read a candlestick chart . Each candle summarizes what the price did during one short slice of time, and the candles side by side show how the session unfolded.

|A candle has a thick body and thin wick.key: |A candle has a thick body and thin wicks above and below it. The body marks where the price opened and where it closed for that period.

|Color tells you direction. A green cand.key: |Color tells you direction. A green candle means the price closed higher than it opened — buyers won that period. A red candle means it closed lower — sellers won. Sellers are nicknamed "bears".

|The wicks show the extremes. The top of.key: |The wicks show the extremes. The top of the upper wick is the highest price reached; the bottom of the lower wick is the lowest . A long wick means price went there and was pushed back.

|One candle is a single data point; the.key: |One candle is a single data point; the sequence of candles is the real information. Several large green candles in a row means buyers are in control. A run of red means sellers are.

|In the simulator, each candle covers a.key: |In the simulator, each candle covers a few minutes of the trading day. Watch them form one at a time to get a feel for the pace. Take the quiz, then your first exercise in the practice arena opens.

|You can read a single candle. Next are.key: |You can read a single candle. Next are the shapes that carry information — reaction candles , which show who won the contest at an important price.

|The hammer : a small body at the top wi.key: |The hammer : a small body at the top with a long lower wick. Sellers drove price down and buyers took it all back before the close. At support, it shows buyers defending the level.
